title: RNA Extraction from Glioblastoma Cell-Line-Derived Spheroids in Atelocollagen Gel
author: Fujita, Imadome, et al.

steps.title: Prepare atelocollagen solution stocks
steps.instruction: Aliquot 500 µL of 4 mg/mL, pH 7.4 3D‑Ready Atelocollagen‑DMEM low‑glucose (Koken) into sterile 1.5 mL tubes on ice, label, and store at –20 °C (up to 1 year).

substeps.instruction: Thaw the atelocollagen bottle in a refrigerator for 8–12 h.
Gather sterile 1.5 mL tubes, 200 µL and 1000 µL pipette tips, and a tube rack.
Fill a bucket with ice, place the tube rack on the ice, and set the tubes in the rack.
Place the atelocollagen bottle on the ice, swirl to homogenize, and keep the bottle on ice while dispensing.
Using chilled pipette tips, dispense 500 µL of atelocollagen solution into each tube.
Label each tube and store at –20 °C (stable for up to one year).

steps.title: Thaw and expand SF126 cells
steps.instruction: Recover a frozen SF126 stock, culture to ~80–90 % confluence in DMEM‑low‑glucose with 10 % FBS and 1 % Pen‑Strep, and incubate for 3 days.

substeps.instruction: Thaw a frozen stock containing 1.25 × 10⁶ SF126 cells.
Resuspend the cells in 10 mL DMEM‑low‑glucose supplemented with 10 % fetal bovine serum and 1 % penicillin‑streptomycin.
Centrifuge at 150 × g for 5 min, discard supernatant, and resuspend the pellet in fresh 10 mL DMEM‑low‑glucose.
Plate the suspension into a 100 mm culture dish.
Incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for 3 days (cells will grow to ~5–6 × 10⁶, ~80–90 % confluence).

steps.title: Form SF126 spheroids in ULA plates
steps.instruction: Generate compact spheroids (8 × 10³ cells per well) in three ultra‑low‑attachment 96‑well plates and monitor formation over 3 days.

substeps.instruction: Confirm that the SF126 monolayer is in logarithmic growth phase (70–85 % confluence).
Aspirate medium gently from the 100 mm dish.
Wash cells with 10 mL sterile pre‑warmed (37 °C) 1 × PBS.
Add 1 mL of 0.5 % Trypsin‑EDTA to cover the cells and incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for 2 min.
Inspect under a microscope to ensure most cells have detached.
Add 5 mL DMEM‑low‑glucose to neutralize trypsin.
Collect the cell suspension into a 15 mL conical tube.
Mix 50 µL of the suspension with 50 µL trypan blue and count live cells using a disposable cell counter.
Centrifuge the suspension at 150 × g for 5 min at room temperature (≈25 °C).
Remove supernatant and resuspend cells to a concentration of 8 × 10⁴ cells/mL with fresh DMEM‑low‑glucose.
Dispense 100 µL (8 × 10³ cells) into each well of three ULA 96‑well plates (one plate for control, two plates for atelocollagen‑embedded test).
Incubate plates at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for 3 days to allow spheroid formation.
On day 3, examine each well with an optimal microscope to verify that a compact spherical structure has formed.
Note: For n = 1 samples, use 1 control plate and 2 test plates; for n = 3, use 3 control plates and 6 test plates.

steps.title: Live‑cell imaging and dispersion analysis
steps.instruction: Acquire time‑lapse phase‑contrast images of control and atelocollagen‑embedded spheroids, then quantify cell dispersion using Incucyte software or the INSIDIA ImageJ macro.

substeps.instruction: Place both control ULA plates (no gel) and test plates (spheroids embedded in atelocollagen gel) into the Incucyte Zoom Live‑Cell Analysis System.
Set the imaging schedule (e.g., every 1 hour) using a 4× objective and run until the predetermined RNA‑collection time point (e.g., 2 days after day 3).
Generate a movie or time‑course image series from the acquired phase‑contrast images.
Quantify the dispersion of invaded cells over time with the Incucyte spheroid analysis software.

If Incucyte software is unavailable, process the phase‑contrast TIFF images with the INSIDIA (INvasion SpheroID ImageJ Analysis) macro: create a binary mask, plot the mask area using the wand tool, and calculate dispersion levels.
